subcutaneous.definition: Under the skin. A subcutaneous injection goes into the layer of fat just below the skin, not into a muscle or a vein.

aseptic-technique.definition: A set of habits that keeps sterile things free of germs while you use them, such as clean hands, a new needle and not touching the needle or the vial top.

sterile.definition: Free of living germs. A needle or a liquid stays sterile only until it touches something that is not sterile.

cellulitis.definition: A bacterial infection of the deeper layers of the skin. The skin becomes red, hot, swollen and painful, and it needs antibiotics. (Doctors in the Netherlands often call a similar infection wondroos.)

abscess.definition: A painful pocket of pus under the skin, usually caused by bacteria. It often needs to be drained by a doctor.

sterile-abscess.definition: An abscess with no germs in it. It is the body's reaction to something in the injected liquid itself. From the outside it looks like an infected abscess.

sepsis.definition: A life-threatening reaction to an infection, in which the body's response starts to damage its own organs. It needs hospital treatment straight away.

lymphangitis.definition: An infection of the lymph vessels, the thin channels that drain fluid from tissues. It shows as red lines running from an infected spot towards the armpit or groin.

necrotising-fasciitis.definition: A rare, fast-spreading bacterial infection of the deep layers under the skin. The pain is much worse than the skin looks, and it needs emergency surgery and antibiotics.

lipohypertrophy.definition: Lumps of thickened fat under the skin where someone has injected many times in the same place. A medicine injected into them is absorbed unevenly.

injection-site-reaction.definition: Redness, itching, pain or a small bruise where the needle went in. A normal one stays small and fades; one that grows may be an infection.

multi-dose-vial.definition: A vial meant to be used several times. It usually contains a preservative, but each time a needle goes in, germs can get in too.

single-dose-vial.definition: A vial meant to be opened once. It usually has no preservative, so whatever is left must be thrown away.

vial-stopper.definition: The rubber top of a vial that the needle goes through. Wipe it with alcohol, let it dry, and do not touch it afterwards.

antimicrobial-preservative.definition: A substance added to a medicine to slow the growth of bacteria after the vial is opened. It does not stop viruses and does not make a contaminated vial clean.

bacteriostatic-water.definition: Sterile water for injection with a preservative (benzyl alcohol) that slows the growth of bacteria. It comes in a container that may be opened more than once.

sterile-water-for-injection.definition: Germ-free water made for dissolving medicines before injection. It has no preservative, so a container is used once and the rest is thrown away.

reconstitution.definition: Dissolving a powdered medicine in a liquid so that it can be injected.

freeze-drying.definition: A way of removing water from a frozen product so that it becomes a dry powder. It helps a peptide keep longer, but it does not kill germs.

cold-chain.definition: Keeping a medicine cold at every step, from the factory to the person who uses it. If one step gets too warm or freezes, the medicine can be damaged.

needle-stick-injury.definition: A prick from a needle that someone has already used. It can pass on blood-borne viruses such as HIV and hepatitis B or C.

post-exposure-prophylaxis.definition: Emergency treatment after a possible exposure to HIV or hepatitis B, for example after a needle-stick injury. For HIV it works best if started within hours, and it no longer works after 72 hours.

blood-borne-virus.definition: A virus that can pass from one person to another through blood, for example on a shared needle. The main ones are HIV, hepatitis B and hepatitis C.

viral-hepatitis.definition: Virus infections of the liver that can pass through blood. Both can become long-lasting and damage the liver; there is a vaccine against hepatitis B.

sharps-container.definition: A hard plastic box with a lid that closes tightly, for used needles. In the Netherlands you can get one at the pharmacy.

klein-chemisch-afval.definition: Dutch name for small amounts of household chemical waste, such as batteries, paint and medicines. Each municipality collects it, for example at a recycling centre (milieustraat) or with a collection van (chemokar).

huisarts.definition: Your family doctor in the Netherlands. You go to the huisarts first for most health problems, and they refer you to a hospital if needed.

huisartsenpost.definition: The Dutch out-of-hours GP service for urgent problems in the evening, at night and at weekends. Call them before you go to a hospital emergency department, unless a life is in danger.

ggd.definition: The Dutch regional public health service. Among other things, it helps after a needle-stick injury and with sexual health, including emergency HIV treatment.

medical-confidentiality.definition: A doctor's duty to keep private what they learn about you as a patient. In the Netherlands there are only a few special situations in which a doctor may or must share it.

contraindication.definition: A situation in which a medicine must not be used because the risk is too high, such as pregnancy or a certain illness. Authorised medicines list them on the label.

anticoagulant.definition: A medicine that makes blood take longer to clot, to prevent dangerous clots. People who take one bruise and bleed more easily.

weakened-immune-system.definition: When the body's defence against germs works less well, for example because of HIV, chemotherapy, steroids or medicines that suppress the immune system. Infections are then more likely and more dangerous.

priapism.definition: An erection that lasts for hours and does not go down, often painful. It is an emergency, because trapped blood can damage the penis for good.

rhabdomyolysis.definition: A condition in which damaged muscle breaks down and releases a protein (myoglobin) into the blood that can harm the kidneys. Signs are muscle pain or weakness with dark, cola-coloured urine.

jaundice.definition: Yellow skin or yellow whites of the eyes. It can be a sign of a problem with the liver, the gallbladder or the pancreas.

melanoma.definition: A type of skin cancer that starts in pigment cells, often in a mole that changes size, shape or colour.

eating-disorder.definition: A mental illness in which eating, weight or body shape take over a person's thoughts and behaviour, for example by eating far too little or by binge eating.

strict-liability.definition: The anti-doping rule that an athlete is responsible for any banned substance found in their body, whether or not they meant to take it.

adrenaline-auto-injector.definition: A ready-to-use pen that injects adrenaline into the thigh during a severe allergic reaction. People with known severe allergies carry one.
